chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who has a debt upon him, and death approaches him, and his heir says to him, 'Your debt is upon me,' he said, 'That frees him, even if his heir does not pay it after him.' And he said, 'I hope that he will not be sinful, and indeed his sin is upon the one who withholds it.'
ai.seo_question: Does a deceased person's debt get cleared if their heir verbally assumes it before death?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a verbal assumption of debt by the heir at the moment of death suffices to absolve the deceased, reflecting the Shia legal principle of *barā'ah* (presumption of innocence) regarding the debtor's final state. This ruling highlights the distinction between the spiritual obligation of the deceased and the practical liability of the heir, ensuring the deceased is hoped to be free of sin even if the debt remains unpaid by the heir.
